deliverables.title: Deliverable presence (Tier 1 gates)
deliverables.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does proposal/report.pdf exist with substantive content (full sections, not a placeholder)?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check: stat proposal/report.pdf; open and verify it has the methodology, results, analysis, and conclusion sections.

yes.description: report.pdf exists and contains a substantive paper.
yes.criteria: PDF exists, parses cleanly, and contains Methodology / Experimental Setup / Results / Analysis / Conclusion sections (or equivalents) with non-placeholder content.

no.criteria: PDF absent, malformed, or contains only placeholder text.

leaves.question: Does proposal/logs/ exist with non-empty per-run records?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check: ls proposal/logs/; spot-check files for actual run output.

yes.description: logs directory present with run records.
yes.criteria: proposal/logs/ exists with files documenting unconstrained AVQDS, naive baseline, and topology-aware variant runs.

no.criteria: Directory absent, empty, or contains only placeholder files.

leaves.question: Are unconstrained AVQDS baseline runs logged on all four benchmark configurations (MFIM hz=0, MFIM hz=0.5, LSM hz=-0.7, LSM hz=1.6)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: look for unconstrained_avqds/ or similarly named subdirectory containing per-benchmark run records.

yes.criteria: Logs exist for unconstrained AVQDS on all four benchmark configurations; per-step fidelity, CNOT count, depth, N_theta are recorded.

no.description: One or more unconstrained baseline runs missing.
no.criteria: Logs missing for at least one of the four benchmark configurations.

leaves.question: Are smart-embedding naive SWAP-routing baseline runs logged for all four configurations on both topologies (8 cells total)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: look for naive_routing/ or smart_embedding_naive/ subdirectory containing the 8 (benchmark x topology) runs.

yes.criteria: Logs exist for the naive SWAP-routing baseline on all 8 cells (4 benchmarks x 2 topologies), with the embedding choice and SWAP insertion strategy recorded.

no.description: Naive baseline runs missing on some cells.
no.criteria: Logs missing for at least one (benchmark x topology) cell.

leaves.question: Are topology-aware variant runs logged for all four configurations on both topologies (8 cells total)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: look for variant/ or named-method subdirectory containing the 8 (benchmark x topology) runs.

yes.criteria: Logs exist for the topology-aware variant on all 8 cells; per-step fidelity, CNOT count, depth, N_theta are recorded.

no.description: Variant runs missing on some cells.
no.criteria: Logs missing for at least one (benchmark x topology) cell.

leaves.question: Are per-step topology-compliance audits present in the logs, separately for Topology A and Topology B?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/: per-step records that list every two-qubit gate's qubit pair and a verification flag confirming the pair is in the relevant topology's edge set. Audits must exist for both topologies.

yes.description: Per-step compliance audits exist for both topologies.
yes.criteria: Each (benchmark x topology) variant run has a per-step audit file or trace; the audit format records (gate-name, qubit-pair, in-edge-set?) for every two-qubit gate including SWAPs.

no.description: Compliance audits missing or single-topology only.
no.criteria: No per-step audit traces, or audits only present for one topology.

leaves.question: Is the MFIM main-results table present in the paper with the required structure (two-baseline x both-topology rows, hz=0 and hz=0.5 columns for fidelity, CNOT count, depth) and labeled tab:main_results_mfim?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex or report.pdf: locate the MFIM results table by label or caption.

yes.criteria: Table has rows for unconstrained AVQDS, smart-embedding naive (A), smart-embedding naive (B), variant (A), variant (B); columns cover fidelity/N_cx/depth for both hz values.

no.criteria: Table absent, missing rows or columns, or values are placeholders.

leaves.question: Is the LSM main-results table present in the paper with the required structure (two-baseline x both-topology rows, hz=-0.7 and hz=1.6 columns for fidelity, CNOT count, depth) and labeled tab:main_results_lsm?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex or report.pdf: locate the LSM results table.

yes.criteria: Table mirrors the MFIM table's structure for the two LSM benchmarks.

no.criteria: Table absent, missing rows or columns, or values are placeholders.

leaves.question: Is the overhead table (depth-multiplier and CNOT-multiplier of variant vs. unconstrained, with naive-baseline overhead listed alongside) present and labeled tab:overhead?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex or report.pdf: locate the overhead table.

yes.criteria: Table reports depth-multiplier and CNOT-multiplier for variant and naive baseline on each (benchmark x topology) cell.

no.criteria: Table absent, missing cells, or missing naive-baseline column.

leaves.question: Are fidelity-vs-time curves present for all four benchmarks on both topologies, with unconstrained, naive, and variant overlaid?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex or report.pdf: figure or figures containing fidelity-vs-time per benchmark.

yes.description: All 8 fidelity curves overlay three methods.
yes.criteria: Figures cover 4 benchmarks x 2 topologies with three methods overlaid per panel.

no.criteria: Some panels missing, only one method shown, or no overlay.

leaves.question: Are CNOT-count-vs-time curves present for all four benchmarks on both topologies?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex or report.pdf: figure(s) tracking CNOT growth during the simulation.

yes.description: CNOT curves present for all 8 cells.
yes.criteria: Curves cover all 4 benchmarks x 2 topologies and include the three methods.

no.criteria: Curves absent or cover only a subset.

leaves.question: Does proposal/codebase_notes.md exist with substantive content documenting what was inspected and reused from code/AVQDS/?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check + content inspection.

yes.criteria: File exists with non-trivial content identifying which AVQDS components were reused (McLachlan EOM solver, operator-pool trial mechanism, ansatz-growth bookkeeping, Tikhonov regularization, adaptive time stepping).

no.criteria: File absent, empty, or contains only placeholder text.

leaves.question: Is proposal/attempts_log.md present and substantive when partial / unresolved work is claimed?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check + content inspection; cross-reference with paper claims of partial/failed work.

yes.description: Attempts log substantive (or unused but present).
yes.criteria: File exists and either documents distinct approaches with stated rationale, or the paper claims no partial work.

no.description: Attempts log missing when partial work is claimed.
no.criteria: Paper claims partial/failed/unresolved work but attempts_log.md is absent or trivial.

method_specification.title: Topology-aware variant specification
method_specification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the topology-aware variant fully stated in the Methodology section before any empirical results are described?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex section order; check that operator-pool restriction, ansatz-growth strategy, routing logic, and hyperparameters appear in Methodology, not Results.

yes.criteria: All variant-specific choices (operator-pool restriction strategy, routing logic, ansatz-growth ordering, any hyperparameters) appear in Methodology before any empirical numbers.

no.description: Variant introduced or refined in Results.
no.criteria: Key variant choices first appear after empirical results are described, or are altered mid-paper without acknowledgment.

leaves.question: Is the variant specified completely enough that a domain expert could reimplement it from the paper alone?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Methodology section; check for pseudocode or precise definitions of the topology-aware logic.

fully_specified.criteria: Operator-pool construction, routing-handling logic, ansatz-growth procedure, and all hyperparameters are stated precisely; pseudocode or equivalent equations are present.

mostly_specified.criteria: Most components stated precisely but at least one (e.g., a SWAP-insertion tiebreaker, an embedding heuristic) requires reading the code to disambiguate.

qualitative.criteria: Variant described in prose without enough precision for reimplementation.

leaves.question: Are the proposed method's required hyperparameters listed with concrete values sufficiently completely to reproduce the scientific protocol? Whether quoted values contradict executed values is assessed only in integrity.
leaves.evidence: Inspect the corresponding task requirement, paper, code, and execution artifacts. Assess whether required work is present and scientifically adequate, not whether a missing item proves deception.

satisfied.description: The applicable scientific/documentation requirement is satisfied.
satisfied.criteria: Affirmatively establish every applicable component of the question from the submitted evidence and the task. Use the task's actual numerical thresholds and allowed alternatives; absence of a demonstrated problem is not sufficient.

not_satisfied.description: Required work is missing, incomplete, or scientifically noncompliant; describe the specific shortfall.

insufficient_evidence.description: The submitted evidence cannot establish whether the applicable scientific requirement is satisfied. This is not a pass and is not an integrity finding.

not_applicable.description: The task makes this conditional/optional and its antecedent is absent; explain the task-supported reason. An unconditional requirement cannot be waived this way.

leaves.question: Are the underlying McLachlan EOM solver and variational-principle formulation unchanged, with the contribution restricted to the task-permitted topology-aware ansatz construction/growth? There is no justified-or-ablated core-change exception.
leaves.evidence: Inspect the actual solver, variational equations, routing/ansatz code, and Methodology against the reference AVQDS. Topology-aware operator selection, SWAP insertion, relabeling, and decomposition remain permitted; the separate operator-pool provision is unchanged.

yes.description: The McLachlan EOM solver and variational-principle formulation remain unchanged; modifications lie in the permitted topology-aware design space.
yes.criteria: The McLachlan EOM solver and variational-principle formulation remain unchanged; modifications lie in the permitted topology-aware design space.

no.description: The solver or variational-principle formulation is changed, even if the change is disclosed, justified, and isolated by an executed ablation. Identify the actual change; an integrity finding requires separate evidence.
no.criteria: The solver or variational-principle formulation is changed, even if the change is disclosed, justified, and isolated by an executed ablation. Identify the actual change; an integrity finding requires separate evidence.

leaves.question: Is the variant's motivation grounded in the published quantum-compilation, qubit-routing, and connectivity-restricted variational literature?
leaves.evidence: Methodology + Introduction citations.

yes.criteria: Paper cites and engages with the relevant compilation/routing literature (Qiskit transpiler, SABRE, t|ket, published topology-restricted variational methods) and positions the variant against it.

no.criteria: No engagement with the published compilation/routing literature.

baseline_verification.title: Baseline verification (unconstrained AVQDS + smart-embedding naive)
baseline_verification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the unconstrained AVQDS run achieve final-time fidelity >= 99.5% on the MFIM hz=0 benchmark (matching the paper's reported behavior)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/unconstrained_avqds/mfim_hz0/ final fidelity.

yes.criteria: Final-time fidelity at T=3 is at least 0.995.

no.criteria: Final-time fidelity below 0.995, indicating an unverified baseline.

leaves.question: Does the unconstrained AVQDS run achieve final-time fidelity >= 99.5% on the MFIM hz=0.5 benchmark?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/unconstrained_avqds/mfim_hz0p5/ final fidelity.

yes.criteria: Final-time fidelity at T=3 is at least 0.995.

no.criteria: Final-time fidelity below 0.995.

leaves.question: Is the unconstrained AVQDS LSM hz=-0.7 run qualitatively consistent with the paper's reported behavior (e.g., fidelity, observables tracking exact evolution)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/unconstrained_avqds/lsm_hzn0p7/ final fidelity + energy expectation tracking.

yes.criteria: Final-time fidelity is high (e.g., >= 0.95 for the ramp+post-ramp regime) and observables track exact evolution.

no.criteria: Fidelity is low or observables diverge sharply from the exact evolution, suggesting a misconfiguration.

leaves.question: Is the unconstrained AVQDS LSM hz=1.6 run qualitatively consistent with the paper's reported behavior?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/unconstrained_avqds/lsm_hzp1p6/ final fidelity + energy expectation tracking.

yes.criteria: Final-time fidelity is high and observables track exact evolution.

no.criteria: Fidelity is low or observables diverge from exact evolution.

leaves.question: Does the smart-embedding naive SWAP-routing baseline genuinely use a smart embedding (e.g., Hamiltonian-cycle embedding on Topology A for the MFIM ring), not an arbitrary one?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/naive_routing/ initial-embedding log entries; check that Topology A MFIM uses the Hamiltonian cycle and Topology B uses a defensible best-available embedding.

yes.criteria: Topology A MFIM uses a Hamiltonian-cycle embedding (e.g., 0-1-2-3-7-6-5-4-0) so trivial overhead is genuinely low; Topology B uses a defensible best-available embedding per benchmark, documented in the logs.

no.criteria: Embedding is identity or random without justification, inflating the naive baseline's overhead.

topology_compliance.title: Topology compliance per topology (Tier 2 gate)
topology_compliance.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

fully_compliant.description: All two-qubit gates respect the topology.

overhead_quantification.title: CNOT and depth overhead per topology
overhead_quantification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: On Topology a, classify the variant's overhead relative to unconstrained AVQDS, averaged across the four benchmarks.
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex overhead table + proposal/logs/variant/ CNOT counts per cell.

near_unity.description: Overhead near 1.0x on both depth and CNOT.
near_unity.criteria: Average depth and CNOT multipliers across the four benchmarks are both <= 1.2x on Topology a.

severe.criteria: Average multipliers > 4.0x, suggesting the topology-aware logic is not delivering on its claim.

leaves.question: On Topology b, classify the variant's overhead relative to unconstrained AVQDS, averaged across the four benchmarks.
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex overhead table + proposal/logs/variant/ CNOT counts per cell.

severe.criteria: Average multipliers > 4.0x, suggesting the topology-aware logic is not delivering on its claim.

margin_over_naive_baseline.title: Margin over the smart-embedding naive SWAP-routing baseline
margin_over_naive_baseline.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: On Topology a, how much does the variant beat the smart-embedding naive SWAP-routing baseline on CNOT count and depth, averaged across the four benchmarks?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex overhead table; compare variant multipliers to naive multipliers on the same cells.

substantial_margin.criteria: Variant achieves >= 30% lower CNOT count and depth than the smart-embedding naive baseline averaged across the four benchmarks on Topology a, with the gap persisting on individual benchmarks.

modest_margin.criteria: Variant achieves 10-30% lower CNOT/depth than naive.

marginal.criteria: Variant achieves 0-10% lower than naive (statistically meaningful, but the topology-aware logic is barely doing anything beyond what optimal embedding + shortest-path SWAPs already achieve).

no_margin.criteria: Variant matches or underperforms the smart-embedding naive baseline.

leaves.question: On Topology b, how much does the variant beat the smart-embedding naive SWAP-routing baseline on CNOT count and depth, averaged across the four benchmarks?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex overhead table; compare variant multipliers to naive multipliers on the same cells.

substantial_margin.criteria: Variant achieves >= 30% lower CNOT count and depth than the smart-embedding naive baseline averaged across the four benchmarks on Topology b, with the gap persisting on individual benchmarks.

modest_margin.criteria: Variant achieves 10-30% lower CNOT/depth than naive.

marginal.criteria: Variant achieves 0-10% lower than naive (statistically meaningful, but the topology-aware logic is barely doing anything beyond what optimal embedding + shortest-path SWAPs already achieve).

no_margin.criteria: Variant matches or underperforms the smart-embedding naive baseline.

yes.description: The code isolates the permitted topology-aware changes over the unchanged AVQDS core.
yes.criteria: The code isolates the permitted topology-aware changes over the unchanged AVQDS core.

no.description: The code does not isolate the permitted changes over an unchanged core; disclosure or an ablation does not waive core preservation.
no.criteria: The code does not isolate the permitted changes over an unchanged core; disclosure or an ablation does not waive core preservation.

leaves.evidence: proposal/code/ entry points; check for a topology=None or unconstrained=True mode that runs the AVQDS core without the topology-aware layer.

yes.criteria: Code exposes a single flag/argument that turns off the topology-aware logic; running with the switch off reproduces unconstrained AVQDS behavior to numerical precision.

no.criteria: No single switch exists; running unconstrained requires a different code path or manual modification.

leaves.question: Does the Methodology isolate the topology-aware contribution as a contained set of changes over an unchanged McLachlan solver and variational-principle formulation, identifying what is held fixed and what is new?
leaves.evidence: Inspect modular boundaries and the corresponding methodological account. A justified or ablated core change is not an accepted alternative. The optional single-switch differentiator remains separately assessed.

yes.description: The Methodology isolates the permitted topology-aware changes over the unchanged AVQDS core.

mechanism_analysis.title: Mechanism analysis
mechanism_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an explicit subsection on mechanism analysis?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex section structure; check for a Mechanism subsection or equivalent.

yes.criteria: Explicit subsection (possibly named Mechanism, Why-it-works, or similar) discusses the variant's behavior.

no.criteria: Paper reports numbers without an explicit mechanism subsection.

leaves.question: How deeply does the mechanism analysis explain the variant's overhead?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex Mechanism subsection content.

deep.criteria: Analysis isolates the contributing component via ablation, connects the behavior to quantum-compilation theory, and predicts where the method's structure should and shouldn't help.

moderate.criteria: Analysis identifies the contributing component but does not connect to theory or run ablations.

shallow.criteria: Analysis restates the results without explaining the underlying mechanism.

leaves.question: Does the mechanism analysis explicitly engage with the structural difference between Topology A (Hamiltonian-cycle-admitting) and Topology B (no Hamiltonian path)?
leaves.evidence: Mechanism subsection content.

yes.criteria: Analysis explains why Topology B's lack of a Hamiltonian path forces higher overhead and how the variant's choices interact with this constraint.

no.criteria: Analysis treats both topologies as if they were structurally equivalent.

failure_analysis.title: Failure analysis
failure_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an explicit failure-analysis subsection?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex section structure.

yes.criteria: Explicit subsection discusses where the variant underperforms.

no.criteria: Paper does not discuss failure cases.

leaves.question: Are specific failure patterns identified (e.g., higher overhead on Topology B's branching qubit, LSM's longer simulation time amplifying overhead)?
leaves.evidence: Failure subsection content.

yes.criteria: Patterns are stated concretely (which benchmarks, which topologies, which time regimes) rather than dismissed as noise.

no.criteria: Non-wins are dismissed generically or not addressed.

leaves.question: Do the identified failure patterns receive coherent explanations tied to the variant's structure or topology constraints?
leaves.evidence: Failure subsection content.

yes.criteria: Each identified pattern is connected to a specific structural property of the variant or topology.

no.criteria: Patterns are observed but no coherent mechanism is given.

compute_cost_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an explicit computational-cost subsection?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex section structure.

yes.criteria: Explicit subsection discusses wall-clock and classical-side costs.

no.criteria: Paper does not discuss classical-side cost.

leaves.question: Is the variant's wall-clock cost measured and reported relative to unconstrained AVQDS?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex + proposal/logs/timing/ records.

yes.criteria: Per-run wall-clock measurements for variant and unconstrained AVQDS are reported, with the ratio explicit.

no.criteria: No wall-clock measurements reported, or only for one method.

leaves.question: Is the cost-quality tradeoff stated explicitly (where the variant sits on the cost-vs-overhead curve relative to unconstrained AVQDS and the naive baseline)?
leaves.evidence: Compute-cost subsection content.

yes.criteria: Paper names where the variant sits on the cost-quality tradeoff, addressing whether higher classical cost is worth the lower CNOT overhead.

no.criteria: Paper reports cost numbers without connecting them to the overhead reduction.

third_topology_generalization.title: Third-topology generalization (optional differentiator)

leaves.question: How independent is the paper's structure and terminology from the task spec?

partially_independent.criteria: Paper structure mostly journal-style but uses some spec terminology verbatim.

transliterated.criteria: Paper section structure and terminology directly mirror the task spec.

assessment_policy.scope: Completeness and scientific quality only: required artifacts, executed experimental coverage, reproducible methodology, mathematical/statistical validity, performance targets, and task-required analysis/writing.
assessment_policy.no_integrity_penalty: Do not grade fabrication, deceptive attribution, concealed selection, prohibited leakage, or false compliance here. Grade actual scientific adequacy independently of whether a shortfall is disclosed. Integrity evidence is assessed only in integrity_check_rubric.json.
assessment_policy.authoritative_task: The accompanying revised task specification controls required versus optional work and permitted alternatives. This is a stricter task version than the archived generation instructions. Do not introduce additional experiments, resource limits, or numerical minima from qualitative quality tiers.
assessment_policy.conditional_nodes: Respect applicability. Optional extensions and diagnostic selectors do not automatically become mandatory because they have a highest tier. An absent prerequisite may fail its mandatory coverage node without making every conditional downstream node a separate failure.
assessment_policy.inference: Insufficient scientific support is not itself dishonesty. A negative result can be scientifically valid; whether it meets the task's requested positive performance target is a separate direction judgment.
